key_insight: APRIL-MedSeg turns medical image segmentation into a flexible, YAML-configurable toolbox where models are built from reusable parts. It unifies many modern training paradigms—such as semi-supervised, domain adaptation, distillation, weak supervision, text-guided segmentation, and foundation-model support—under one modular framework.
problem_solved: Medical image segmentation research often uses fragmented codebases and task-specific implementations, making it hard to compare methods, reuse components, and extend to new paradigms. This paper addresses the need for a unified, extensible, and reproducible framework for 2D medical segmentation.
method: Decomposes segmentation networks into modular, reusable components managed through a YAML-driven configuration system.
Uses a registry-based design with inheritance to simplify model, training, and experiment customization.

Integrates multiple advanced learning paradigms in one toolbox, including semi-supervised learning, domain adaptation, knowledge distillation, weakly supervised learning, text-guided segmentation, and foundation model support.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, APRIL-MedSeg lowers the barrier to experimenting with state-of-the-art segmentation strategies and comparing them fairly. It can speed up research, improve reproducibility, and make it easier to adapt medical segmentation systems to new datasets and supervision settings.

paper_title: APRIL-MedSeg: A Modular Medical Image Segmentation Toolbox Embracing Modern Paradigms
paper_authors: Juntao Jiang, Jinsheng Bai, Linxuan Fan, Yali Bi, Jiangning Zhang
